title: Ned Calls Out
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — a wordless story for sharing and talking through together; there are no sounds to decode yet.
note_for_grown_ups: A true animal fact tucked into this story: baby ducklings really do call out loudly when they lose sight of their family, and the adults listen for exactly that sound to find them.

pages.talk_prompt: Ned is following behind Moss and Olive through the tall grass — can you see he is falling a little behind?
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling waddling behind Moss the hedgehog and Olive the owl through tall green grass, a little way behind them.

pages.talk_prompt: The grass has closed in all around Ned — what do you notice has happened to his friends?
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling surrounded by tall green grass stems, looking around, his friends no longer in sight.

pages.talk_prompt: Ned has opened his beak wide — what do you think he is doing?
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling standing with his head up and beak wide open, calling loudly, sound shown as pale rippling lines in the air.

pages.talk_prompt: Olive has turned her head sharply — what do you think she has just heard?
pages.illustration: Olive the owl turning her head sharply in flight, listening intently towards a sound coming from the grass.

pages.talk_prompt: Olive is flying back towards the sound — where do you think she is heading?
pages.illustration: Olive the owl flying low and fast back over the tall grass towards where the calling sound came from.

pages.talk_prompt: Ned has been found — how do you think he feels now that his friends are back?
pages.illustration: Olive the owl landing beside Ned the duckling in the grass as Moss the hedgehog arrives too, Ned looking relieved.
